title: find_enclosing_hook_case false-positives on any nested case inside the hook gate
evidence:
+    flag_indent = indent_of(lines[flagged_idx])
+    for i in range(flagged_idx - 1, -1, -1):
+        line = lines[i]
+        if hook_case in line and indent_of(line) < flag_indent:
+            return True
+        if indent_of(line) < flag_indent and re.search(r"\bcase\b|\}", line):
+            if re.search(r"^\s*case\b", line) and hook_case not in line:
+                return False
detail: A legitimate `case other { ... [RefcheckTakeOver] ... }` nested inside `case call.hooks.can_take_over` hits the inner non-hook case first and returns False, failing CI. Contradicts the docstring's 'nearest hook_case opener' claim.
recommended_fix: Track brace/case nesting depth and only accept a hook-case opener at the depth of the flagged block's chain.

title: Em-dash scanner toggles string state on escaped quotes, enabling false negatives
evidence:
+    in_str = False
+    for i, c in enumerate(cleaned):
+        if c == '"':
+            in_str = not in_str
+        elif c == EM_DASH and in_str:
+            return True
detail: Unlike strip_comments, this loop ignores backslash escapes: a `\"` inside a string flips state, so an em-dash later on the line can be missed. One escaped quote is enough to break the state.
recommended_fix: Skip the character following a backslash when toggling in_str, mirroring strip_comments.

title: Whole-line log-call exemption lets a same-line user-facing em-dash evade the ban
evidence:
+LOG_CALL_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(log_error|log_warning|log_info|log_debug|log_critical|log_fatal|console\.\w+)\("
+)
+    cleaned = strip_comments(line)
+    if LOG_CALL_RE.search(cleaned):
+        return False
detail: Any line matching a log call is exempted wholesale, even if the call text sits inside a string literal alongside a user-facing em-dash. The console.* alternative is dead (only .gleam files are scanned).
recommended_fix: Exempt only the call argument span, not the line; drop the console.* alternative.
